keyFindings.description: The shipped envoy_publish description — rendered verbatim to OpenCode agents by packages/envoy-plugin/src/server.ts:12,70,135, rebuilt into packages/claude-envoy/dist/envoy-channel.js, and repeated as the docs-site row docs/site/src/content/docs/dispatch/envoy.md:123 — says an ad-hoc topic 'reaches the sessions subscribed when it is published, yours included'. For a session the listener delivers to by push it reaches nobody: packages/envoy-plugin/src/server.ts:93 registers with a serve port and no selfSubscribed, so packages/envoy/internal/session/session.go:62 takes the push branch, and no ad-hoc topic is ever fanned out — the listener's only core subscription is notifications.role.> (cmd/listener/main.go:733) and its durable filters to bus.StreamSubjects() (cmd/listener/durable.go:123,45). Such a session subscribes (cmd/listener/api.go subscribeHandler stores the interest with no warning) and then receives nothing, silently, with no delivery exception and no log line. skills/envoy/SKILL.md:143-145 and packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:2196-2203 carry exactly that caveat; the two texts above do not. Both thermonuclear agents raised it independently. Fix: one clause in the shared description and the docs row, then `bun run check-dist` in packages/claude-envoy so the bundle matches.

'a subagent's publish to a topic the session that spawned you subscribes to' mixes the third person with the second inside one clause, in a paragraph whose whole job is to be unambiguous. The tester recorded the same observation. Not a defect; worth one word while the file is open.
